node-1.label: Patient presented with left-sided nasal obstruction for 1 year

node-2.label: Patient is in their 40s with a medical history of sleep apnea and diabetes, no history of immunosuppression, and negative serum HIV test results

node-3.label: Bilateral nasal endoscopy revealed an excised mass with an aggregated size up to 7.0 cm in its greatest dimension

why.why: Histopathology demonstrates a malignant plasmacytic infiltrate with plasma cell markers and EBER positivity, which is not compatible with a benign sinonasal tumor. MRI evidence of bone erosion also argues against a benign process. Therefore, the benign sinonasal tumor hypothesis is essentially excluded, decreasing confidence from 0.4 to 0.02.

Both the pathologist and radiologist independently affirm that the histopathologic and MRI findings establish a malignant sinonasal tumor; the immunophenotype excludes carcinoma and B-cell lymphoma, and the bone marrow is negative. These expert analyses reinforce the malignant diagnosis, so confidence is raised from 0.98 to 0.99.

Although EBER positivity suggests EBV involvement, the histopathological features—diffuse large atypical plasmacytic infiltrate with CD138, MUM-1, and lambda restriction—are diagnostic of plasmablastic lymphoma, a malignant neoplasm, not a chronic inflammatory/infectious mass. MRI bone erosion further supports an aggressive malignant process. Thus, chronic inflammatory/infectious mass is highly unlikely, decreasing confidence from 0.15 to 0.01.
